pr_title: Fix Duplicate Rows on Deep Sorting
pr_body:
**TL;DR: Add support for deep sorting using Strapi queries.**

**Initial report:**  [https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/11892](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/issues/11892)

### What does it do?
- Add the support for deep sorting in the Strapi query builder
    - [If an attempt to deep sort is detected](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/fix/duplicates-on-deep-sorts/packages/core/database/src/query/query-builder.ts#L449-L475), then [wrap the current query with one allowing for deep sorting capabilities](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/fix/duplicates-on-deep-sorts/packages/core/database/src/query/query-builder.ts#L626).
    - Detecting whether to use deep sort is done by checking the `orderBy` clauses.
        - Only look at those having at least one `.` character.
        - If, when divided into groups, one of them (*expect for the last*) matches one of the join table aliases or a relational attribute in the current metadata, then it means we’re facing a deep sort.
    - How the wrapping works (code available [here](https://github.com/strapi/strapi/blob/fix/duplicates-on-deep-sorts/packages/core/database/src/query/helpers/order-by.ts#L86-L216)):
        1. Initiate a new Knex query instance (referenced as `Q`) using the DB connection.
        2. Clone the original query to create the sub-query (referenced as `R`) and avoid any mutation on the initial object
            1. Remove pagination statements
            2. Remove select statement
        3. Create a sub-query callback from `R` to extract and sort partitions using row number, known as `T` 
            1. Partition by `R.id`
            2. Order by the original clauses
        4. Create the final `Q` query, that selects and sorts the wanted data using `T`
            1. Re-apply the pagination
            2. Re-apply a clean select
            3. Re-apply the order by using data returned by `T`
        
        Here’s the difference in the generated queries and returned rows (before/after)
        
        - Before
        
        ```sql
        SELECT DISTINCT "t2"."name",
                        "t0".*,
                        "t0"."id"
        FROM "public"."articles" AS "t0"
        LEFT JOIN "public"."articles_categories_lnk" AS "t1" ON "t0"."id" = "t1"."article_id"
        LEFT JOIN "public"."categories" AS "t2" ON "t1"."category_id" = "t2"."id"
        ORDER BY "t2"."name" ASC
        LIMIT ?
        ```
        
        | name | id | document_id | title |
        | --- | --- | --- | --- |
        | Category A | 3 | czdpldaa2eynfjd95pbh2rf5 | Article D |
        | Category B | 1 | ls4i55fi1zdkiwiwq427qutw | Article A |
        | Category C | 4 | eb3wgthmh8kjwua5t2rqgahz | Article B |
        | Category D | 2 | efppopmjiovgck66adwpvntv | Article C |
        | Category D | 3 | czdpldaa2eynfjd95pbh2rf5 | Article D |
        | Category D | 4 | eb3wgthmh8kjwua5t2rqgahz | Article B |
        - After
        
        ```sql
        SELECT "t3".*,
               "t3"."id"
        FROM "public"."articles" AS "t3"
        INNER JOIN
          (SELECT "t4"."id",
                  "t4"."__strapi_order_by__t2_name",
                  row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY "t4"."id"
                                     ORDER BY "t4"."__strapi_order_by__t2_name" ASC) AS __strapi_row_number
           FROM
             (SELECT "t0"."id",
                     "t2"."name" AS "__strapi_order_by__t2_name"
              FROM "public"."articles" AS "t0"
              LEFT JOIN "public"."articles_categories_lnk" AS "t1" ON "t0"."id" = "t1"."article_id"
              LEFT JOIN "public"."categories" AS "t2" ON "t1"."category_id" = "t2"."id") AS "t4") AS "t5" ON "t5"."id" = "t3"."id"
        AND "t5"."__strapi_row_number" = 1
        ORDER BY "t5"."__strapi_order_by__t2_name" ASC,
                 "t5"."id" ASC
        LIMIT ?
        ```
        
        | id | document_id | title |
        | --- | --- | --- |
        | 3 | czdpldaa2eynfjd95pbh2rf5 | Article D |
        | 1 | ls4i55fi1zdkiwiwq427qutw | Article A |
        | 4 | eb3wgthmh8kjwua5t2rqgahz | Article B |
        | 2 | efppopmjiovgck66adwpvntv | Article C |
    - **Performances** ⚡
        - Before: 6 rows retrieved starting from 1 in 61 ms (execution: 5 ms, fetching: 56 ms)
        - After: 4 rows retrieved starting from 1 in 51 ms (execution: 4 ms, fetching: 47 ms)
        - ⇒ **No noticeable changes in performances**

*(other changes)*

- Add API tests for sorting and deep sorting:
    - **Regular Sort**: This tests the basic sorting of articles by title.
    - **Deep Sort (1st level)**: This tests sorting of articles when they are nested one level deep, specifically sorting articles based on category names.
    - **Deep Sort (2nd level)**: This is a more complex sort, checking sorting of articles based on tags' names which are two levels deep.
    - **Deep Sort (2nd level) + Regular Sort**: This test checks the correct sequence of sorting when multiple sorts (a deep sort and a regular sort) are applied.
    - **Two Deep Sorts (2nd and 1st level)**: This test checks the correct sequence of sorting when multiple sorts (two deep sorts) are applied.
    - **Deep Sort (2nd Level) + Pagination**: Tests sorting on paginated results.
    - **Deep Sort (1st Level) + Filters**: Tests sorting on filtered results.
    - **Update + Deep Sort**: Ignore sorting on update operations
    - **Delete + Deep Sort**: Ignore sorting on delete operations
- Fix flaky API tests on PostgreSQL
    - `deep-filtering.test.api.js` was incorrectly querying collectors by using `$contains` instead of `$contains` to filter by cards’ names.
    - `number-of-draft-relations.test.api.js` was running create operations concurrently, which was causing an issue with transactions when updating the relation attached to the entities (e.g. transferring ownership)
    - Fixed fixtures being JSON files with hardcoded ID, causing the sequences for PK (in PostgreSQL) to be out-of-sync and generate uniqueness violation. They’ve been moved to JS modules and use callbacks to reference other fixtures.
- Fix `createDocumentSiblingsIDSubQuery` in `regular-relation.ts` (database)
    - Use sub-queries instead of re-using the same connection (and mutating it)
    - Support attaching the same transaction to the sub-queries.

### Why is it needed?

Deep sorting causes duplicate results in the returned rows.

This is due to the conflict between needing to select the column used in the order by statement and applying the distinct to it, creating duplicate rows.

### How to test it?

Run the `sort.test.api.ts` suite or try running Strapi queries (REST or programmatically) containing deep sorts (e.g. `categories.tags.name`)

### Related issue(s)/PR(s)

fix #11892

Take over #20125, #20124, #13387

---
Shoutout to @innerdvations and @MorganClt for their help :slightly_smiling_face:

issue_context.title: [v4] sort by graphql duplicating rows
issue_context.body:
## Bug report

### Describe the bug

Graphql sort on nested relations is basically duplicating rows as a join would do.
This was working in v3.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Create your graphql query on a resource that has a relation. This is a one to many in this case, this should work for any relation i think
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12382966/145875139-6c35a982-2145-42ad-b8a6-f300eaf9a03b.png)

Call this in your sort parameters:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12382966/145875198-7df2f9b2-a47a-41d8-9bea-44105940d34c.png)

### Expected behavior

Should only have one row per item but this is duplicated:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12382966/145875347-61f3bb05-b552-421f-96c7-b5ce9c163bda.png)

As you can see there i have multiples rows with the same id depending on the number of nested articles linked to the category.

### System

- Node.js version: 14.18.1
- NPM version: 6.14.15
- Strapi version: 4.0.0
- Database: MySQL
- Operating system: Windows 11
comments: Is it the same when you request data through REST API?

Yes it is:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12382966/146079585-7e85683a-877c-4096-a8d7-ea27c138dd9f.png)

I don't believe this is possible as I'm looking at the sort code and I believe sort can only be at the parent level (you can sort the relational data itself but you can't sort the parent data on the relational responses.)

Looping in @strapi/maintainers here as I'm honestly not sure.
(Tested and validated the above doesn't work, nor does something like this:

@GautierDele Unfortunately, still happening on the latest version...
@akasummer for almost a year i forgave, this wont be fixed for such a major problem. Either you find an alternative or you find another solution

This is also a problem with the REST API, not only GraphQL.

I'd call it a gamebreaker...

Steps for me to reproduce:
Have a "post" with "categories"
Call sth. like "/api/posts?pagination[limit]=4&sort=categories.id"
A post that has just one category will return the post just once.
A post that has two categories will return just once.
A post that has at least three categories will return multiple times.

Edit: Just to make things clear… What i really would like to do is sorting my posts by its number of categories. But there is no sorting option for that why i used to make it work with categories.id in strapi v3.
This is a real problem. Why isn't this solved yet ?

@LapX this is considered a rather complicated issue, fixing it correctly on the DB level would require a different solution for every database we support. We just didn't get the time or priority to move forward with it yet.

Issue is still there, for example a `Product` which has many `prices` (relations) in different currencies
```js
{ sort: { prices: { amount: 'asc' } }, filters: { prices: { currency: 'usd' } } }
```
It's returning duplicated products, looks like filters are ignored, is there a way to make something like post-filtering?

We also started experiencing this issue 2 weeks ago.
Today we realised that the problem was in some custom code in the lifecycle hooks of the Content-Type.

So I would recommend giving a look at your lifecycle hooks if you have any.
Same issue here. Hope that it will be fixed soon.
